v0.6.name: Crew
v0.6.features:
Agreed with the player (stages 1-3 done). Build ALL of these:

CARRY-OVERS
- Realistic deadhead airlines: prefer the low-cost carrier based at the origin/destination (Ryanair at STN/DUB/BGY..., easyJet at LGW/LTN/GVA..., Wizz at BUD/OTP..., Vueling at BCN, Transavia at ORY/AMS...), then airlines of the origin/destination country, then hub connections; never put an airline on a route it doesn't realistically fly (known bad picks: STN-DUB on Aer Lingus instead of Ryanair; LDE-LIS on easyJet; TFS->OTP via IST). Add tests over a sample of route pairs.
- Pacing tune: bot seed 2 gets only 1.4 meaningful actions/week (target >= 1/week on every seed incl. 1-6, ideally ~2) and governments pay late only 2/5 (target 'mostly late'). Tune offer/decision pacing and government late-payment odds without making the game easier.

1. ROSTER BOARD: a crew x day grid like a real crew-control screen: rows = crew (grouped by base/rank/type, filterable), columns = days (zoom week <-> month, scroll), cells show duties (flight numbers/route), days off, standby, sick, training/conversion, joining, positioning and deadheading, using the same colours/labels as the v0.5.2 crew calendar. Drag and drop a duty from one crew member to another to swap/reassign, with live FTL legality while dragging (green ok / red illegal with the reason) and the existing manual-assignment rules (locked assignments survive re-plans). iPad touch first (long-press to pick up, drag, drop), large targets, smooth scrolling with ~120 crew x 31 days.

2. BULK TYPE-RATING CONVERSION (replaces the bigger 'training & currency' idea; keep it simple): the player selects many crew at once (multi-select in the Crew list and on the roster board) and sends them on a type conversion to another aircraft type (e.g. A320 -> A330). The game groups them into classes automatically: pilots in pilot classes, cabin crew in cabin classes, max 20 per classroom (overflow makes additional classes, staggered if needed). Pilots take much longer (realistic: ~5-7 weeks incl. ground school, simulator and base/line training) than cabin crew (~1-2 weeks). Each class shows on every member's roster as a block labelled e.g. 'Conversion A330' (in the crew calendar strip, the roster board, and the Crew list status). Costs per head (pilots much more expensive) go through the ledger. While converting they can't fly; after completion they hold the new rating (decide and document whether they keep the old one — realistic for cabin crew to hold up to 3 types, pilots usually one type unless common type rating like A330/A350 or A320 family). Planning UI shows start/end dates, who's in which class, cost, and warns if it leaves the current fleet short of legal crew.

3. MORALE & ATTRITION: morale (already 0-100 on crew) is driven by tour length, days off, time away from base, hotel standard, per-diem policy, late-notice roster changes and mission type (evacuation/humanitarian lift morale; deportation/controversial flights lower it); company policies the player sets (hotel standard, per-diem level, max tour length) trade money for morale. Low morale raises sick calls, lowers service (affects client satisfaction/reputation slightly) and eventually crew resign with a notice period (shown on the roster and in the inbox) so the player must re-hire. Visible on crew cards, a company-wide morale indicator, and clear inbox messages. Balance: noticeable but not punishing when the player is reasonable.

4. EXTRA CREW ABOVE THE LEGAL MINIMUM: per aircraft (and optionally per contract) the player can set extra cabin crew above ceil(seats/50) (and an extra pilot where useful). Extra crew cost salary/per diem, improve crew morale (lighter workload) and service quality (client satisfaction, small reputation effect), and some clients (VIP, sports, long-haul) request or pay for it. The auto-roster honours it; legality and costs follow.

v0.7.name: Fleet & Ladder
v0.7.features:
Agreed with the player (stages 1-3 done). Build ALL of these:

CARRY-OVERS FROM v0.6 READINESS (fix first)
- Bulk conversion modal: when a red 'fleet short of legal crew' warning is shown, Book must ask for an explicit confirm (one tap must never ground the fleet).
- Roster board perf at 4×: memoise rows per crew/version or throttle refresh to ~1 Hz while the clock runs (p99 was 50 ms with 4× CPU throttle).
- Deadhead carriers still unrealistic in places: DXB–LIS on TAP (TAP doesn't serve DXB; Emirates does), LIS–SOF and HAM–BOJ via SOF on Bulgaria Air, LGW–GVA on Swiss (easyJet flies LGW–GVA). Add per-airline reach/avoid lists (hubs, bases, realistic networks) and a test table of ~40 route pairs with the expected carrier.
- Pacing: seed 2 has 41/52 active weeks (target ≥ 42); loosen the quiet-week floor slightly.
- Flaky timing test under load in board.test.ts/roster.test.ts: widen the budget or make it deterministic.

6. SCARCE AIRCRAFT MARKET: used aircraft for sale, dry-lease-in offers from real lessors, rare new-delivery slots, and lease returns at the end of leases (return conditions and costs). Offers are scarce and stay open for days; deliveries take weeks to months. A bought/leased aircraft is DELIVERED AT THE SELLER'S/LESSOR'S LOCATION (a real airport somewhere in the world), appears there on the map, and the game plans a FERRY flight to the player's base (pilots only, shown on the map as a ferry with its path, with fuel/crew costs and FTL; tech stops if range requires). The DELIVERY PILOTS first DEADHEAD on real commercial airline flights from their base (or wherever they are) to the aircraft's location, and those commercial flights are shown on the map exactly like the v0.5.2 crew deadheads (grey icon, floating flight-number label e.g. 'TP 1342', thin grey dotted path, tap for airline/flight no./route/times/time to landing/crew on board), with connections as separate legs; then they fly the delivery ferry home. Their rosters show the deadhead + ferry + rest. A Settings toggle turns ON/OFF a notification (inbox + quiet toast, optional auto-pause) whenever a new buying/leasing option appears on the market.

7. CABIN RECONFIGURATION: all-economy, two-class or VIP layouts per aircraft; a refit takes the aircraft out of service for days-weeks (at a capable MRO station) and costs money; the layout changes seats and decides which contracts it can bid for (VIP/sports want premium cabins, Hajj/troop rotations want max seats); feasibility explains it; shown on Fleet cards and the Schedule.

8. THE LADDER (approvals & bigger aircraft): an approvals tree — ETOPS 120 -> 180 -> 240, widebody operations, long-haul with augmented crews, ultra-long-haul (FRMS) — each needs time, money, trained/rated crew and a clean record; approvals gate which aircraft types and contracts are available, unlocking the 767/A330, then the 777, then the A350-ULR and prestige long-haul work. Clear progression UI (a tree/ladder on the Company screen with requirements and progress) and goals that celebrate each step.

v0.7.1.name: Crew Control
v0.7.1.features:
Agreed with the player (stages 1-3 done). Build ALL of these. (The v0.6.2 hotfix already fixed deadhead reachability: planOut/outTicket() in crew/timeline.ts searches all ticket times and gives exact reasons — build on it, don't regress it. ALSO switch ops/events.ts crewReadyAt (crew-short wait estimates) from the old 3 h-buffer guess to outTicket().)

CREW SHORTAGE AS A SERIOUS SITUATION ('Crew Control'):
1. WARNING LADDER: amber warning when a shortage is detected (up to ~48 h ahead), escalating to red + auto-pause (existing crewShortage pause setting) at ~12 h to departure; a clear 'CREW SHORTAGE' banner on the flight (map panel, schedule block, Up Next) and in the top bar's pause badge; inbox message with the flight, missing seats and time left. (A distinct crew-shortage SOUND comes with the v0.9 sound set — leave a hook.)
2. CREW CONTROL PANEL (opened from the warning/badge/flight): shows exactly which seats are missing (e.g. 1 CPT, 2 CC) and the ranked SOLUTIONS, each with cost, timing and consequences, one tap to apply, with a preview of what changes:
   a. AUTO-FIX: re-run the auto-roster for this flight (and its pairing) and show what it changed.
   b. DEADHEAD SOMEONE: candidate list with each person's commercial itinerary, arrival time and legality after it (uses the v0.6.2 logic).
   c. DELAY UNTIL CREW ARRIVES: new departure time, delay cost / client penalty and knock-on effects on later legs (ripple), confirm.
   d. PRIVATE JET POSITIONING: charter a business jet to fly the crew to the departure airport. Available ANY TIME, priced so it only makes sense when urgent (realistic charter rates ~5-8k USD per flight hour incl. positioning of the jet itself; light/midsize/heavy jet by crew count and range; departs within ~2-3 h from a nearby FBO). ON THE MAP it shows exactly like the commercial deadheads (floating label, thin dotted path, tap panel with times/time to landing/crew aboard) BUT with its own small BUSINESS-JET icon and the label/panel naming a chartered private jet (e.g. 'Private jet · Citation XLS' or a realistic charter operator name) instead of an airline. Rosters show it as a positioning/deadhead block. Costs through the ledger.
   e. CALL IN STANDBY / DAY-OFF CREW: overtime pay and a morale hit (v0.6 morale system).
   f. COMMANDER'S DISCRETION: extend the FDP by up to 2 h where legal (existing applyDiscretion), with fatigue/morale effect.
   g. SWAP CREWS: take a crew set from another flight and show what that flight then needs.
   h. SUB-CHARTER TO A RIVAL: a rival flies it at their price (existing subcharter).
   i. CANCEL: penalty and reputation hit.
3. The bot uses Crew Control sensibly; balance stays in band; old saves load.

PLAIN-LANGUAGE ISSUES (player request, agreed 'try all 8, refine later'; the player is a former cabin crew member, not a planner: NO jargon lists, ONE simple story per problem, visual aids). Apply to every crew problem (crew shortage, illegal/tight crew, 'can't reach', rest, FDP, sick, resigned):
4. 'WHAT'S WRONG?' CARD, always the same four lines, shown on the Crew Control panel, the flight sheet, the duty modal and the inbox message: WHAT ('AWQ816 has no pilots'), WHY in one sentence a layperson understands ('Your free pilots are in Lisbon and the earliest they can land in Düsseldorf is 11:40, 3 h after the latest 08:34'), DOES IT HURT? (money + passengers + delay, e.g. 'Not much: empty flight, ~3 h late, no penalty' or 'Yes: 180 passengers, $42K penalty'), WHAT YOU CAN DO (the solution buttons). One main cause only; details behind a 'Details' tap.
5. REACH TIMELINE BAR for 'can't get there in time': a horizontal bar with now, must-land-by, report, departure, earliest arrival; the gap drawn in red; labels in UTC and local.
6. GAUGES for the limits: a fuel-gauge style bar for FDP ('Day length 10:45 of 11:00'), rest ('Rest 7:30 of 10:00 by 06:00'), 7-day/28-day block hours; green/amber/red; shown per crew member in the duty modal and on the card when the cause is a limit.
7. MINI-MAP on the card for location/positioning causes: the crew member's dot, a dashed line to where they're needed, the flight (airline or private jet) they would take, with times.
8. ONE REASON PER PERSON in the candidate list and Adjust crew, with an icon: wrong place / needs rest / day too long / busy on another flight / sick / not rated / on leave. Pick the ROOT cause (a pilot busy on another trip is 'busy on AWQ815 to London until 10:30', never 'At LIS, not DUS'). Tap the person for the full list.
9. TAP-TO-EXPLAIN GLOSSARY: tapping FDP, deadhead, positioning, tight, discretion, ACMI, wet lease, sub-charter, AOG, standby, rest, block hours shows a one-line plain meaning (small popover, dismiss by tapping elsewhere). Terms are rendered via one <Term> component so the glossary is one table.
10. 'DOES IT HURT?' SEVERITY in money and passengers on every crew warning and inbox message (badge: 'no cost', '$12K', '180 pax', '2 h late').
11. COLOUR LEGEND in Schedule, Roster board and the map crew layer (small '?' button): what red, amber, grey, dotted and solid mean.
(Already fixed in v0.6.3/v0.6.4, in the tree: flightCrewStatus confirms stored illegal/tight marks live via crewIssuesFor/liveCrewLevel — keep it.)

PLAIN LANGUAGE EVERYWHERE (player: 'inside v0.7.1'): extend the same four-line card, <Term> glossary and severity badges to EVERY kind of problem:
12. MAINTENANCE: AOG, check due/overdue, check booking clashes, no slot ('CS-THB can't fly: a brake fault in Lisbon. Repair ~9 h. Hurts: 2 flights, 230 passengers, $38K'), with a timeline bar (fault → repair → next flight) and a gauge for check intervals ('A-check: 82% used').
13. CONTRACTS: feasibility warnings on offers (crew short, aircraft busy, range, cabin mismatch, paint), counter-offer expiry, change requests, penalties, cancellations — one plain sentence each + what it costs + the button that fixes it.
14. MONEY: cash warnings, overdue invoices, loss months, lease/deposit due, covenant/goal misses: the card says what happens if ignored and the exact date.
15. AIRCRAFT/DELIVERY: delivery delays, ferry, refit, lease return conditions.
16. INBOX: every warn/bad message carries the card (collapsed) and a severity badge; a filter 'Problems only'; tap 'Explain' on any message.
17. GLOSSARY SCREEN under Settings: all terms with one-line meanings and a 'show me' link to where they appear.
18. A 'WHY?' button on every red/amber dot anywhere (schedule, fleet, crew, map) that opens the card.
19. First-time hints: the first time each kind of problem appears, a one-paragraph plain explanation with a picture (the same visuals), 'don't show again'.
Keep: calm visuals, iPad landscape, real names, speeds 1/2/4 only. Bot and balance unchanged; old saves load.

ALSO: add a v0.7.1 entry at the top of src/data/whatsNew.ts (features + improvements in player words; it drives the 'What's new' pop-up) and set CURRENT accordingly; update the Title footer version via that data.

v0.7.2.name: Crew Rules & Fleet
v0.7.2.features:
Agreed with the player (their own list, stages 1-3 done; the player is a former ACMI flight attendant: get the rules right). Build ALL of these:

PLAYER FIXES FIRST (player notes 22 Oct; build these before the rest; screenshot of the top bar in .handover/updates/topbar-space.jpg):
F1. HOTEL DOT: the white crew-at-hotel dot on the map stays while ANY crew member is still at that station (resting, waiting for a ticket, between duties of a tour); today it disappears when the duty completes. Remove it only when the last one leaves.
F2. MARKET ALERTS: move the market-alerts toggle (and its pause-on-offer toggle) from Settings into the Market section of the Fleet screen. A new market offer also shows in the TOP BAR WARNING AREA next to the 1×/2×/4× control, the same place and style as the crew-shortage warning (tap → the offer). Settings keeps nothing about it.
F3. SUB-CHARTER RELIABILITY: sub-chartering must hurt reliability noticeably and progressively (a client notices when its flights are flown by someone else): per sub-chartered leg a reliability cost that grows with how many legs were sub-chartered in the last 90 days (e.g. −0.3 for the first few, rising to −1 per leg when a third or more of a contract's legs were sub-chartered), shown on the sub-charter option's chips and in the plain-language card ('Hurts: reliability −2 · the client notices'). Keep the bot in band.
F4. CONTRACT NAMES: no more repetitive 'Thursday series DUS–FUE' / 'Monday series'. Name series after what they are, with variety and real flavour: tour operator programme names ('TUI summer programme Düsseldorf–Fuerteventura', 'Jet2 weekend rotation', 'Sunweb ski charters Amsterdam–Salzburg', 'Corendon Antalya flights'), events, seasons, sports, the client's own words; the weekday stays in the details, not the title. A big varied pool per archetype; never the same title twice in a row for a client.
F5. CABIN CREW JOIN IN 1 WEEK: hiring flight attendants (PUR/CC — v0.7.2 ranks) takes ~7 days to join (pilots keep their longer lead). Update the hire modal text, bot and balance.
F6. CABIN REFITS START STRAIGHT AWAY: a refit can start as soon as the aircraft is free (no 7-day hangar lead; the first offered slot is the next free window from today, not weeks out); the refit modal lists the earliest slots first and says plainly why a later date is needed if the aircraft is busy.
F7. UP NEXT MORE COMPACT: smaller panel; remove the legend under it (each row already names its type); rows closer together in a tidy grid with thin horizontal AND vertical divider lines (time | flight/reg | route | type), like a departures board; at most ~5 rows; collapsible.
F8. TOP BAR LIVE STRIP (player asked for suggestions; build this default, they can refine): use the empty space between the speed control and cash (see screenshot) for a calm live OPS STRIP: warnings first on the left (crew shortage, market offer, AOG — existing), then compact live facts: 'Airborne 3/5' (aircraft in the air of fleet), 'Next: AWQ717 LHR→CGN in 1:20', 'On time today 92%', 'Crew: 14 on duty · 6 at hotels'. Each item taps through to its screen (Map/Schedule/Crew). Updates at most once per game minute, no flicker or scrolling ticker; shrinks gracefully at Safari width (1180×750) by dropping the lowest-priority items.

1. EASA FTL RESEARCH FIRST: before coding, research and write docs/acmi/EASA-FTL.md from the real rules (Regulation (EU) 965/2012 Subpart FTL, ORO.FTL.205 FDP table by report time and sectors, ORO.FTL.210 cumulative limits (60 h/7 d, 110 h/14 d, 190 h/28 d duty, 100 h/28 d and 900 h/yr block (1000 h/calendar yr)), ORO.FTL.235 rest (min 12 h at home / 10 h away, or the preceding duty length if longer; weekly 36 h recovery with 2 local nights within 168 h), split duty, standby, commander's discretion (2 h, 3 h with augmented crew), in-flight rest extensions by rest facility class (class 1 bunk / class 2 seat flat in a separate area / class 3 economy seat with 40° recline, curtain, leg rest) and augmented-crew FDP (CS FTL.1.205: 3 pilots: 14/15/16 h by class; 4 pilots: 15/16/17 h; cabin crew FDP extension with in-flight rest). Same rules for pilots and cabin crew where EASA says so (cabin crew report may be earlier; cabin crew FDP counted from their earlier report). Then make the engine's crew/rules.ts match the researched tables (a REGRESSION-SAFE change: old saves load; the bot stays in band; tests pin the tables). Keep this doc as the reference for every later crew update.

2. CAPTAINS CAN FLY AS FIRST OFFICERS when short staffed and needed (never an FO as captain): the auto-roster only does it when no FO is available, the duty picker lists captains for an FO seat under a 'Captain flying as FO' label; captain pay stays; a small morale hit for the captain when it happens more than twice a month. Shown on the roster/flight sheet as 'CPT (as FO)'.

3. CREW REST COMPARTMENTS: each aircraft type/variant carries whether it was sold with a crew rest compartment (bunks: class 1) — widebodies may have it or not per airframe (market listings and the fleet card show 'Crew rest: bunks / none'); short-haul types never. With a compartment, FDP extends per the EASA class-1 table (augmented crews). Without one, the CABIN CONFIGURATION (v0.7 refit feature) offers 'Crew rest seats': block off the LAST ROW of economy (curtain; class 3) — these seats STILL COUNT as passenger seats and sell when the duty needs no in-flight rest; when a duty needs in-flight rest they are blocked and the sellable seat count drops for that flight (shown on the flight sheet and in contract feasibility). Class 3 gives the smaller extension per the table. The ladder's augmented-crew/ULR approval uses the real class.

4. CABIN CREW RANKS: remove CSD and SCC. Only two cabin ranks: PUR (Purser, senior cabin crew member / SCCM) and CC (junior cabin crew). Every complement has exactly 1 PUR (SCCM) + CC; widebodies may add a second PUR as deputy only if the type's minimum says so. SAVE MIGRATION: existing CSD and SCC crew become PUR; existing pairings/slots/contracts/requirements/offers that mention CSD/SCC are rewritten; nothing is lost; tests load an old save and check it. Rename everywhere in the UI, docs and bot.

5. HIRING FLIGHT ATTENDANTS WITH MULTIPLE TYPES: in the hire screen the aircraft-type choice for cabin crew is a set of TICK BOXES (hold A320 family, A330, 767, 777...), not a dropdown; price and joining time scale with the number of types; the existing 'up to 3 types' rule applies; staffing views show per-type coverage. Pilots keep one type (rating) as today.

6. SELL OWNED AIRCRAFT AND RETURN LEASES EARLY: Fleet card → 'Sell' for owned aircraft with a market value from age, hours/cycles, check status and cabin (quote from the v0.7 market model; sale takes days; cash in; contracts on it must be covered or sub-chartered first — warn). 'Return early' for leased aircraft: early-return fee + return check condition from the v0.7 lease-return feature; the game suggests the LEAST USED aircraft (lowest utilisation last 90 days) when the player asks 'which one?'. Both appear in the fleet list with a plain-language card (v0.7.1 style).

7. REAL-WORLD C-CHECK HUBS: C-checks happen at real MRO hubs by type, not at base (cabin retrofits still happen at home base): e.g. 767 → Miami (ex-euroAtlantic practice), 777 → Amman (Joramco), A330 → France (Bordeaux-Mérignac / Châteauroux), A320 family → Sofia or Malta (Lufthansa Technik), 737 → Budapest or Shannon, A380/A350 → Toulouse / Manila; pick 1–2 per type at your discretion from real MROs, with the hub's price level. The pilots FERRY the aircraft to the hub, DEADHEAD home on commercial flights (shown on the map like other deadheads), and at the end of the check DEADHEAD back to the hub and FERRY the aircraft home — all rostered and costed automatically when a check is booked; the check modal shows the hub, ferry times and the deadhead tickets; A-checks stay at base/line stations as today.

8. 'WHAT'S NEW' POP-UP: first launch after an update (after the loading screen, on the home screen) shows 'Version X is live!' with the new features and improvements of that version (a data file per version), 'Got it'; shown once per version (settings.seenWhatsNew), reopenable from Settings → 'What's new'. (First shipped with v0.7 by the orchestrator; keep the data file updated for every version from here on.)
Keep: calm visuals, iPad landscape, real names, speeds 1/2/4 only, old saves load, bot in band.

v0.7.3.name: In-flight Rest & EASA
v0.7.3.features:
Agreed with the player (22 Oct): they supplied an authoritative EASA FTL reference guide (current Oct 2026) and asked to 'study it and apply it to the game; in-flight rest and the rest classes available on each plane must be a BIG thing; correct any parameters that might be wrong'. SOURCES (read both in full before designing): the guide /home/user/wt/notes/.handover/updates/EASA-guide-2026-10.txt (it is the authority; where it and anything else disagree, the guide wins) and the read-only audit of the v0.7.2 tree /home/user/wt/notes/.handover/updates/EASA-audit-v0.7.2.md (sections 0, A = every parameter MATCH/WRONG/MISSING with file:line, B = rest facilities per aircraft type with proposed shares/bunk counts and the data model, C = the visible in-flight rest feature, D = contradictions in the v0.7.2 docs, Appendix = order of work). Line numbers in the audit may have moved: re-locate before editing. Build ALL of this:

1. CORRECT EVERY WRONG PARAMETER AND CITATION (audit A + D + Appendix steps 1–2): fix EASA-FTL.md and code comments/citations (ED Decision 2014/002/R + 2023/023/R; Table 1/2/3/4 names; CS FTL.1.205(b)/(c) letters; ORO.FTL.215 positioning; etc.); drop the cabin rest table's extra 18:01–18:30 row (table ends at 17:31–18:00 = 3:50; cabin caps 18:00/17:00/16:00 by class 1/2/3); commander's discretion only for unforeseen circumstances at or after report (never offered for planned duties; +2 h, +3 h augmented in all texts; base = basic FDP; rest after ≥ 10 h); rest after ANY augmented FDP ≥ preceding duty or 14 h; consecutive night duties computed with at most 4 sectors; contract feasibility uses the real max FDP for the report time (not a flat 13 h) and the aircraft's rest classes. Keep EASA-FTL.md the single reference, rewritten to match the guide.

2. IN-FLIGHT REST AS A BIG, VISIBLE FEATURE (audit B + C, player's top priority):
   a. Separate PILOT and CABIN CREW rest facilities per airframe with class 1/2/3 and number of places (FCRC bunks, overhead CCRC, A330/A340 lower-deck module LDMCR, curtained business seats = class 2, crew rest recliners with leg rest = class 3; a plain economy row is NOT class 3). Realistic per-type shares and bunk counts from audit B2; market rolls them per airframe; save migration per audit B3 (old {bunks, seats} → new model; nothing an old save relies on becomes illegal).
   b. restPlan(): a deterministic per-duty in-flight rest plan (audit C2): cruise windows, pilots 90 consecutive min each and 120 for the landing pilots, max 3 sectors, 'cruise too short → no extension', cabin crew minimum rest from the CS FTL.1.205(c)(3) table by FDP band and cabin class, service constraints (half the cabin crew stay in the cabin, no rest in the first 90 / last 60 min), extra cabin crew when needed, seats blocked only on flights that need rest. pickAugment, complement(), feasibility and the bot all use it.
   c. Where the player sees it (audit C3): fleet card + market listing show 'Pilots rest: … · Cabin crew rest: …' and 'Longest day: 16 h with 3 pilots · 17 h with 4 (18 h on one long sector)'; market filter 'Has bunks'; a small static bunk glyph on the aircraft art where the compartment really is (no animation); flight sheet 'In-flight rest' section with a calm static timeline of who rests when, where and how long (pilots by name, cabin crew in groups), verdict chip and the blocked-seats line; duty modal 'Day length X of Y · Why Y?' explanation incl. the cabin crew band; offer modal per-aircraft line (✓ / needs 4th pilot / needs refit); roster board bed icon + 3P/4P on augmented duties.
   d. Plain-language cards (v0.7.1 four-line format) for restFacility, restTooShort, cabinRest, restSeats (audit C4) with one-tap fixes (swap aircraft, 4th pilot, more cabin crew, plan a refit) and glossary terms (class 1/2/3 rest, FCRC, CCRC, lower-deck crew rest module, in-flight rest, landing pilots, augmented crew).
   e. Refit options (audit C5): curtain off business seats (class 2), crew rest recliners (class 3, incl. A321LR/757), lower-deck crew rest module for A330/A340, flight crew rest compartment for 767/A330 (MRO, best combined with a C-check at the v0.7.2 hubs), overhead rest for big twins; each shows 'Opens: 16 h days with 3 pilots (was 15 h)'.
   f. Contracts: long-haul and ULR offers state the rest they need; ULR needs class 1 for both pilots and cabin crew; prices/feasibility/bot follow (audit C6).

3. THE MISSING RULES (audit Appendix 4–5, 7), each with tests, plain-language cards and rostering that respects them: planned extension +1 h (CS FTL.1.205(b) table incl. 3/4/5-sector columns and 'not allowed' cells, max 2× per 7 days per crew member, sector limits by WOCL encroachment, +2/+2 or +4 h rest, not with in-flight rest or split duty); delayed reporting (CS FTL.1.205(d) <4 h / ≥4 h / ≥10 h rules); disruptive schedules early/late type (pick one, documented) + late/night → early needs 1 local night + 4+ disruptive → 60 h recovery; 2 local days twice a month; time-zone compensation table CS FTL.1.235(b)(3)(i) and 3 local nights between alternating E/W rotations; away rest after ≥4 h zone difference ≥ duty or 14 h; split duty (CS FTL.1.220) and standby/reserve (CS FTL.1.225/230) as simplified-but-correct rules where the game uses them (at least: split duty available to the roster for long ground breaks; airport/home standby counting rules for the v0.7.1 call-in fix).

4. 'WHAT'S NEW' entry for v0.7.3 at the top of src/data/whatsNew.ts.
Keep: calm visuals, iPad landscape, real names, speeds 1/2/4 only, old saves load (migrations tested), bot in band (seeds 1–6), the rules readable by a former cabin crew member.

v0.8.name: World
v0.8.features:
Agreed with the player (stages 1-3 done). Build ALL of these:

0. CLIENT RELATIONSHIPS THAT MATTER (player notes 22 Oct: favours such as an extra leg do nothing today; contracts should start poor and get better as you build relationships): every client has a visible relationship level (e.g. New → Known → Trusted → Partner) built by on-time flying, accepted change requests and favours (extra legs, short-notice cover, waiving a small penalty) and hurt by cancellations, sub-charters and late recoveries. Higher levels bring real rewards: better rates (+3–15 %), longer/bigger contracts, first refusal before rivals, faster payment, repeat and exclusive offers, forgiving small delays, and client-specific messages. A NEW COMPANY STARTS WITH POOR WORK (short, low-margin, odd hours, unloved routes, demanding clients) and better offers unlock as reputation and relationships grow. Show the level and its effect on each offer ('Trusted client: +8 % rate') and on a Clients view on the Company screen; plain-language card for why a client is unhappy.

9. MORE CONTRACT TYPES: Hajj airlifts (big seasonal pilgrim flights; dates drift ~11 days earlier each year with the Islamic calendar; max-seat cabins), UN multi-year rotations, VIP & presidential (high pay, high standards, premium cabins, extra crew), deportation flights (well paid; hurt reputation and crew morale — a moral choice), war-zone evacuations (war-risk insurance cost, danger, urgency), medical/air-ambulance style charters, music tours (multi-city routing), Antarctica flights (special approvals/runways). Each with realistic pay, requirements, feasibility explanations and flavour text with real clients.

10. RIVAL OPERATORS WITH PERSONALITIES: real ACMI operators (Hi Fly, Wamos Air, euroAtlantic, Getjet, Airhub, Avion Express, Titan Airways, Privilege Style, Air Atlanta Icelandic, Heston, KlasJet, Smartwings, Global Crossing...) each with a style (aggressive pricing, prestige, reliability, size), fleets that change over time, competing bids so the player sometimes loses work to a cheaper/closer rival (with an explanation), and sub-chartering BOTH ways (hire a rival when stuck; rivals ask the player to fly for them). A rivals view on the Company screen.

11. MARKET CYCLES: fuel price moves (affects charters/ferries and some offers), seasonality (summer peak, winter trough, Hajj season), and demand shocks (an airline collapse creates ACMI demand; recession lowers it); visible as a simple market outlook and in offer volume/pricing.

12. INVENTED WORLD EVENTS: coups, strikes, volcanic ash, natural disasters, airline failures, wars, airspace closures, etc. in real places involving real airlines/governments (the player explicitly wants invented events — BRIEF 'Player decisions'); they create urgent work (evacuations, AOG/ACMI demand), risks (airspace closures reroute or cancel flights, insurance) and opportunities, announced in the inbox and on the map (e.g. a shaded closed airspace).

13. DRY LEASE CONTRACTS (player request): the client leases the aircraft only — our pilots deliver it (ferry to the client's base, deadhead home on the map) and at the end collect it (deadhead out, ferry back); no crew from us during the lease; monthly lease income + hourly reserves; the client's hours accrue on our airframe (checks still ours, booked around the lease); the client may fly it in their own livery/paint (v0.5.1 paint); risk of late return / damage events. Feasibility and plain-language card.

14. MIXED-CREW CONTRACTS (player's real case: Getjet A330 for Air Senegal — 8 cabin crew, only 2 from Getjet): the client provides part or most of the CABIN CREW (never pilots): the contract says 'client provides N of M cabin crew' (half, most, all-but-the-purser...); our roster only fills our share (always at least the PUR unless the contract says the client's SCCM leads); lower price per block hour accordingly; morale/language/standards flavour; the roster board shows client crew as grey placeholder seats.

v0.9.name: Experience
v0.9.features:
Agreed with the player (stages 1-3 done). Build ALL of these:

5. UNLOCKABLE AUTOMATION (department heads earned through achievements; the player wants to struggle first and feel accomplishment): Ops Control duty manager (unlock: 25 sectors with no illegal duty) handles routine delays and sick call-ins with the player's default rules; Maintenance planner (unlock: first C-check completed on time) auto-books A-checks into maintenance nights; Crew scheduling desk (unlock: 2 months at >= 98% crew coverage) repairs the roster after disruptions and manages extra crew; Commercial analyst (unlock: 5 contracts completed) scores offers vs the fleet and suggests counter-prices; Credit control (unlock: first late government payment collected) chases late payers and sets terms; Fleet & positioning planner (unlock: first widebody) proposes ferry/positioning plans and tech stops; Custom alert & auto-pause rules (unlock: reputation 'Reliable'). Each is a hire with a monthly salary and a skill level that can make mistakes, can be overridden or switched off, and never takes the big decisions (which contracts, which aircraft, crises). Unlock moments are celebrated.

14. ACHIEVEMENTS, SOUND & TUTORIAL HINTS (sound now fully specified in S below; it overrides the sound wording here): achievements for milestones (with a gallery on the Company screen and calm unlock toasts); calm optional sound and ambient audio generated with WebAudio (no audio files needed unless tiny ones are justified): soft UI clicks, inbox chime, cockpit-style ding for decisions, a DISTINCT urgent sound for CREW SHORTAGE (the player already chose it: see S), faint airport/cabin ambience — all with a Settings master switch and volume, OFF by default if autoplay rules require; gentle first-time tutorial hints per screen (dismissible, 'don't show again', reset in Settings), written for an ACMI insider (no condescension).

S. AVIATION SOUND SET (player, 23 Oct; calm sounds for calm situations, urgent sounds for urgent ones). Synthesize with WebAudio so they sound like real airliner cabin/cockpit chimes: sine/triangle partials with a natural bell decay and slight room reverb. No harsh beeps. These meanings are fixed by the player:
- HIGH chime (single, soft): routine info, e.g. a new inbox message or a crew member joined.
- LOW chime (single, soft, like the seat-belt ding): calm timeline events, e.g. a flight departed or landed (off by default as too frequent; toggle), pause and resume.
- HIGH-LOW chime (the classic two-tone 'bing-bong'): NEW CONTRACT offer arrived; a softer variant when a contract is signed.
- DOUBLE high-low: MEDIUM emergency, a decision needed soon, e.g. AOG, a delay with penalty risk, a sick call, a late payer, an offer about to lapse, a world event touching our flights.
- TRIPLE high-low: SERIOUS emergency, e.g. a flight about to be cancelled, airspace closed on an active flight, cash below zero, an evacuation request, a client relationship collapsing.
- URGENT ALARM (distinct, master-caution style, short and repeated a few times, never endless): used ONLY for CREW SHORTAGE and CREW OUT OF HOURS. Both share this one sound.
- The rest is up to you. Examples:
  - achievement unlocked: a warm ascending three-note chime;
  - department head hired or unlocked: a pleasant flourish;
  - soft UI clicks and toggles;
  - optional faint ambience (airport terminal or cabin hum), OFF by default.
Each event maps to exactly one sound, in a single table in code (src/ui/sound.ts or similar), and is documented in docs.
- Volume and settings:
  - Rate-limit and merge bursts: at 4× speed never machine-gun chimes; play the highest-priority sound once per short window.
  - Settings: master on/off, master volume, and per-category toggles (alerts, chimes, UI clicks, ambience).
  - A 'Test sounds' list where each sound can be played with its meaning.
  - iOS/Safari: unlock audio on the first tap. Respect the silent switch where the browser does.
  - Default ON at a moderate volume after the first tap, except ambience, which stays OFF.

T. CREW OUT OF HOURS (new alert, player request): a separate alert and plain-language card for when a pilot or flight attendant has reached a legal limit (FDP or duty, cumulative 7/28-day or 12-month hours, or rest not met), distinct from CREW SHORTAGE (a seat with nobody to fill it).
- It gets its own inbox and alert type and its own icon.
- The four-line card says who, which limit, by how much, and the fixes (replace, delay for rest, sub-charter...).
- Crew Control handles it like a shortage.
- It uses the URGENT ALARM sound (same as crew shortage).

U. COMMANDER'S DISCRETION IS NEVER PLANNED (player, ex-cabin crew; EASA ORO.FTL.205(f)): discretion is only for UNFORESEEN circumstances at or after reporting, decided by the commander near the end of the duty as an emergency measure. It can never be counted in planning or agreed when signing a contract.
- Audit everything and make sure discretion is excluded from:
  - 'Longest day' (fleet card, market, refit preview, popover);
  - contract feasibility and pricing;
  - the roster planner;
  - trip moves;
  - offer generation (no impossible offers);
  - restPlan.
- In Crew Control, offer 'Commander's discretion' only after the crew has reported and only for an unforeseen delay. It is never offered before report or for a planned schedule, and the reason is shown in plain words.
- The fleet card's 'Longest day: 13 h · up to 17 h' means extra pilots resting on board. Make the popover say so plainly and say that discretion is never planned.

V. GAME-WIDE LANGUAGE PASS (player request: 'a lot of redundancy'). Go through every player-facing string (cards, offer and feasibility lines, inbox, toasts, glossary, What's new, tooltips, Crew Planning verdict lines) and remove repetition and filler. Plain, short, insider-correct aviation English. Never lose information.
- Known examples:
  - 'You can't fly Corendon's Winter sun to Corfu for Corendon as it stands' (client named twice);
  - the Crew Planning verdict line repeating the numbers shown right above it.
- Keep the four-line card format.
- Produce a before/after list of the main changes in the update doc.

W. CREW SLIP AT A FUEL STOP (player said yes): on a long one-way flight with a tech stop, a fresh crew is positioned to the stop by airline ticket and takes over, so the duty day splits in two. Examples: Dili→Lisbon via PNH+OTP; Madrid→Singapore via IST.
- The slip crew rests in a hotel at the stop as needed.
- Offers that are too long for one crew become flyable with a slip, priced in (tickets, hotel, extra crew). The v0.8 'no impossible offers' rule then counts a slip as a valid plan.
- Feasibility shows 'Crew change at IST (fresh crew flies in)'.
- The roster plans it, and the map shows the slip crew's deadhead.
- Plain-language explanation in the glossary.

X. WHAT'S NEW CATCH-UP (player won't play v0.8 before v0.9): on the first launch of v0.9, the pop-up shows v0.9, v0.8 and v0.7.4 (everything newer than v0.7.3), newest first. This is a one-time catch-up even if v0.8's pop-up was already seen. Afterwards it is the normal rule.

Y. SMALL FOLLOW-UPS FROM THE v0.8 RELEASE:
- A departure delay can make an augmented cabin crew rest plan impossible after the aircraft left. The pre-departure check stops at report time; it must re-check at departure and fix or alert (crew out of hours).
- 747-400 economics: make sure a well-chosen big job (Hajj, troop, UN, full charters) is profitable for an old 747 without making it generally easy. Today the bot loses about 20% on general work with it.
- The bot runtime target (12 s) is still missed: profile and speed up if cheap.


R. ROSTER PLANNING LIKE A REAL EASA OPERATOR (player, 23 Oct: 'Crew has way too many off days, should be mostly standbys including out of base. Learn EASA roster planning guidelines and plan accordingly'). Today the roster gives a small fixed standby pool (BAL.standby, 1 per role per family per day) and every unassigned day becomes OFF, so crews sit at home far too much.
- Study first: the player's guide .handover/updates/EASA-guide-2026-10.txt (standby, reserve, recurrent extended recovery rest, cumulative limits, 'single day free of duty' and Directive 2000/79/EC, AMC1 ORO.FTL.205(f) on standby/reserve availability at bases and hubs). Write a 'Roster planning' section in docs/acmi/EASA-FTL.md with citations: ORO.FTL.110 (rosters published 14 days ahead), ORO.FTL.210 (60 h/7 d, 110 h/14 d, 190 h/28 d duty; 100 h/28 d, 900 h/year, 1,000 h/12 months flight time), ORO.FTL.225 + CS FTL.1.225 (airport standby counts in full; other standby max 16 h and counts 25 % towards duty; standby + FDP awake caps; FDP reductions after 4 h / 6 h), ORO.FTL.230 + CS FTL.1.230 (reserve), ORO.FTL.235(d) (recurrent extended recovery rest of at least 36 h including 2 local nights, never more than 168 h apart, and 2 local days twice a month), Directive 2000/79/EC (at least 7 days a month and 96 days a year free of all duty and standby, notified in advance; 4 weeks paid annual leave).
- New roster rule: days OFF are only the legal and contractual minimum, planned like a real crew-planning department:
  - the recurrent 36 h / 2 local nights at least every 168 h, and twice a month 2 local days;
  - at least 7, and in practice about 8–10, free days a calendar month;
  - at least 96 a year;
  - annual leave blocks spread over the year.
  Days off are notified in the 14-day published roster and protected: a player change that breaks one needs a confirm, and it costs morale.
- Every other non-flying day becomes STANDBY, not OFF:
  - home standby at the home base (other standby, 16 h max windows, early/late split to cover the day's departures);
  - airport standby only where a base's departures justify it;
  - some reserve days where the operator uses them.
- OUT-OF-BASE STANDBY (player's ACMI reality): crews detached to a long-term base or season base (e.g. Dublin for Aer Lingus) and crews night-stopping or waiting downroute sit on HOTEL standby at that station between duties instead of being OFF. Crew Control can then call them for a sick call or disruption there.
  - Show it on the roster board with a distinct label/colour (e.g. 'SBY DUB (hotel)').
  - It costs hotel and per diem as already modelled for detachments.
- Standby counts in the cumulative duty limits (25 % for other standby, 100 % for airport standby), applies the FDP reductions and awake caps when called, and gives rest per ORO.FTL.235 after standby without call-out.
- Crew Control's 'Call in standby crew' and the auto-fix use this larger standby pool first, home and out-of-base, before tickets, delays or jets. Standby call-outs are the normal, cheap fix, as at a real operator.
- Balance and morale: standby pay and allowances if the game models them, otherwise keep salary; small morale effects for many consecutive standbys versus generous days off, documented. Re-check sets.ts / staffing() so 'sets needed' still reflects real planning, not the old OFF-heavy pattern. If the old '5 sets per aircraft' assumption changes with this, explain why in the Planning view in one line.
- Roster board: OFF, SBY (home), SBY (hotel, station), ASBY (airport), RES and leave are clearly distinct. The Crew screen's per-person calendar shows the same. A month view summary per person: days off x of 7 minimum, standbys y, flying z.
- Tests:
  - no crew member ever gets fewer than the legal free days or a recurrent rest gap over 168 h;
  - unassigned days are standby, not off;
  - out-of-base standby is created at detachments;
  - standby counts towards 7/14/28-day duty correctly;
  - call-outs respect the reductions.
- Save migration: existing rosters are re-planned from the next unpublished day; already published days stay as they are.
